description: Production DR posture for the two MRAP-backed bucket pairs (houserx-customer-data-prod-mrap, fdb-clinical-data-prod-mrap), the platform Global Accelerator, and the platform RDS cross-region replica. Primary us-east-2, DR us-east-1. Note the region each metric family actually lives in: S3 replication metrics are published in the DESTINATION bucket's region, Global Accelerator publishes only to us-west-2, and RDS replica metrics only exist in us-east-1. All resource names are pinned to terraform-production; there are no dashboard variables.

panels.description: Max S3 replication latency for each MRAP bucket. RTC target is 15 minutes; sustained values above that mean the replication SLA is breached. Queried in us-east-1 because S3 publishes replication metrics in the destination bucket's Region.
panels.title: S3 replication latency (max)

panels.description: Peak objects queued for replication over the dashboard window. A backlog that does not drain is the earliest sign replication is stuck. Reduced with max rather than last: when replication is keeping up the latest datapoint is always 0, which hides the spikes.
panels.title: S3 ops pending replication (peak)

panels.description:
Seconds houserx-platform-db-production-replica (us-east-1) trails houserx-platform-db-production-10-25 (us-east-2). Shows the latest datapoint, not the window peak, because the RPO question is how much data you lose failing over right now.

RDS publishes ReplicaLag as whole seconds, so 0 means 'under one second', not 'zero'. It is the expected steady state here and is not a broken panel. Treat it as an RPO of <1s, not an RPO of 0. Use the byte-based slot lag panel below to see movement that is invisible at this resolution.

RDS reports -1 in this metric family when lag cannot be determined (for example a disconnected replica), which is why negatives are mapped to UNKNOWN in red rather than falling into the green band.
panels.title: RDS replica lag (latest)

panels.description: Endpoints the platform-production accelerator considers unhealthy. Non-zero on the primary endpoint group means traffic is at risk of being shifted.
panels.title: GA unhealthy endpoints
S3 replication for MRAP buckets: us-east-2 -> us-east-1 (metrics published in us-east-1, the destination Region)

panels.description: ReplicationLatency is reported in seconds and only exists because the replication rules enable RTC + metrics (platform_s3_replica.tf). S3 publishes it in the destination bucket's Region, so this queries us-east-1 even though the source buckets are in us-east-2.
panels.title: Replication latency

panels.description: Objects accepted for replication but not yet replicated. Should return to zero between writes.
panels.title: Operations pending replication

panels.description: Byte volume still queued. Pair with the operations backlog: a large byte backlog with few operations means a handful of very large objects, which is usually benign.
panels.title: Bytes pending replication

panels.description: Objects S3 could not replicate. Any non-zero value needs manual remediation; failed objects are never retried automatically. Unlike the other three replication metrics, this one is published in the SOURCE bucket's Region, so it is queried in us-east-2 (verified via cloudwatch list-metrics).
panels.title: Operations FAILED replication

panels.description: Reverse replication (us-east-1 replica back to us-east-2 primary), configured in platform_s3_replica.tf. Destination here is the us-east-2 primary, so these metrics are published in us-east-2.
panels.title: Reverse replication (us-east-1 -> us-east-2)
MRAP backing buckets - drift between regions

panels.description: houserx-customer-data-prod-mrap. Multi-Region Access Points publish no CloudWatch metrics of their own, so MRAP health is inferred from the two buckets behind it. A size gap that does not close is the practical MRAP-level failure signal. BucketSizeBytes is a once-daily metric with up to 48h delay, so this panel overrides the dashboard range to 30 days.
panels.title: customer-data: bucket size

panels.description: fdb-clinical-data-prod-mrap. Same reasoning as the customer-data panel: divergence between the two backing buckets is the only region-level health signal available for an MRAP.
panels.title: fdb-clinical: bucket size

panels.description: A persistent object-count gap means objects are being written but never replicated, which the latency graph will not show once the pending-operations metric resets. Daily metric.
panels.title: customer-data: object count

panels.description: Object count on each side of fdb-clinical-data-prod-mrap.
panels.title: fdb-clinical: object count
Global Accelerator - platform-production (metrics published only in us-west-2)

panels.description: Healthy vs unhealthy endpoints per endpoint group. us-east-2 is primary (traffic dial 100), us-east-1 is DR (traffic dial 0). Both groups run health checks continuously, so DR going unhealthy is visible here even while it carries no traffic.
panels.title: Endpoint health by endpoint group

panels.description: New connections per endpoint group. This is where traffic is actually landing: during a failover us-east-2 should fall to zero and us-east-1 should pick up. Global Accelerator only emits metrics while requests are flowing.
panels.title: New flows by endpoint group (traffic dial in practice)

panels.description: Bytes in and out of the accelerator, split by endpoint group.
panels.title: Processed bytes

panels.description: TCP resets. Accelerator-generated resets usually mean a listener/endpoint misconfiguration or a security group blocking the flow; endpoint-generated resets usually mean the ALB behind the accelerator is overloaded or draining.
panels.title: TCP resets

panels.description:
Replica lag in seconds, reported by houserx-platform-db-production-replica in us-east-1. This is the data-loss window if you promote the replica right now.

Published as whole seconds, so a flat line at 0 means lag is under one second and is the normal steady state, not a dead panel. Real lag shows up as brief spikes of a few seconds. Gaps in the line mean the replica stopped publishing, and a dip below zero means RDS could not determine lag; neither is a zero-lag condition, and both colour red. For sub-second movement use the byte-based slot lag panel to the right.
panels.title: Replica lag (us-east-1)

panels.description:
WAL not yet consumed by the slowest replication slot, reported by the primary. Unlike ReplicaLag this keeps climbing when a replica disconnects entirely, and it is what eventually fills the primary's storage.

A few hundred MB steady state is normal and does not contradict a replica lag of 0. A physical slot holds restart_lsn back for the replica's needs, so bytes sit in the slot even while replay is current. Watch the trend, not the absolute value: flat is healthy, monotonically climbing is not.
panels.title: Primary WAL retention (us-east-2)

panels.description: CPU on both sides. A replica pinned at high CPU while the primary is idle usually means replay is the bottleneck, which shows up as growing replica lag.
panels.title: CPU: primary vs replica

panels.description: Free storage on both instances. The replica running out of space stops replication silently from the application's point of view.
panels.title: Free storage: primary vs replica

panels.description: Write throughput on the primary drives how much WAL the replica has to consume. Use it to explain lag spikes that correlate with batch jobs.
panels.title: Write throughput: primary vs replica
